item.research_question: How can uniformly dispersed high-entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA-NPs) be synthesized on granular supports (e.g., carbon, Al2O3, zeolite) without phase separation, overcoming the limitations of conventional fixed-bed pyrolysis?
item.material_system: Denary (MnCoNiCuRhPdSnIrPtAu), quinary (FeCoPdIrPt, CuPdSnPtAu), and other multi-element (up to 10 elements) HEA-NPs supported on graphene oxide (GO), carbon black, γ-Al2O3, and zeolite (Permutit)
item.processing_route: Fast moving bed pyrolysis (FMBP) following wet impregnation: Metal chlorides coordinated with 1,10-Phenanthroline loaded on supports; quartz boat pushed into a 923 K furnace zone at 20 cm s−1 (reaching 923 K within 5 s); annealing for 120 min at 923 K under Ar (100 sccm) or H2 (100 sccm) for oxide supports
item.test_conditions: Electrochemical hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in 1 M KOH (pH 13.8) at 10 mA cm−2 and 100 mA cm−2; stability tested via chronopotentiometry for 150 h; structural characterization via HR-STEM, HAADF-STEM, EDX, XRD, XPS, and ICP-OES
key_findings: HEA-NPs achieved a narrow size distribution of ~2 nm up to denary compositions at 923 K
FMBP ensures simultaneous pyrolysis of mixed precursors, preventing phase separation unlike fixed-bed pyrolysis (FBP) which yields phase-separated alloys
FeCoPdIrPt@GO exhibited an overpotential of 42 mV at 10 mA cm−2, lower than commercial Pt/C (64 mV)
Mass activity of FeCoPdIrPt@GO at 100 mV overpotential was 9.1 mA μgPt, 26 times higher than Pt/C (0.35 mA μgPt)
Long-term stability of 150 h maintained at 10 mA cm−2 with no obvious change in morphology or composition
Atomic ratio error in synthesized alloys was below 15%, confirmed by EDX and ICP-OES
Tafel slope for FeCoPdIrPt was 82 mV dec−1, indicating the fastest kinetics among tested samples
item.mechanism: The rapid heating to 923 K within 5 s creates high supersaturation of monomers, leading to a small critical nucleus radius (r* = 0.313 nm) and low critical excess free energy (ΔGr* = 2.54 × 10−20 J). This thermodynamically favors the formation of small, homogeneous nuclei clusters without phase separation, whereas slower heating (FBP/SMBP) results in larger nuclei and phase segregation due to higher ΔGr*.
item.limitations: The text notes that HEA-NPs with low loading (3 wt%) were too small for clear EDX mapping, requiring higher loading (10 wt%) for elemental analysis; also, annealing times of 30 min led to carbon wrapping, while 180 min caused significant particle growth.
item.future_work: The authors propose a scalable method for production of supported HEA-NPs and suggest the strategy opens a venue for synthesizing alloys with tunable compositions for applications in catalysis, chemical sensing, biology, and energy conversion.
quotes: Fast moving bed pyrolysis strategy ensures the mixed metal precursors rapidly and simultaneously pyrolyzed at high temperatures, resulting in nuclei with a small size.
The FeCoPdIrPt@GO exhibited a low overpotential (ɳ) of 42 mV at the current density of 10 mA cm−2, which was much lower than that of the commercial Pt/C (ɳ10 = 64 mV).

The high stability of the quinary HEA-NPs toward HER was related with entropic stabilization, which leads the thermodynamic stable state, thus, preventing adequate driving forces from degradation of HEA-NPs.

records.text: Paper card. Question: How can uniformly dispersed high-entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA-NPs) be synthesized on granular supports (e.g., carbon, Al2O3, zeolite) without phase separation, overcoming the limitations of conventional fixed-bed pyrolysis?. System: Denary (MnCoNiCuRhPdSnIrPtAu), quinary (FeCoPdIrPt, CuPdSnPtAu), and other multi-element (up to 10 elements) HEA-NPs supported on graphene oxide (GO), carbon black, γ-Al2O3, and zeolite (Permutit). Processing: Fast moving bed pyrolysis (FMBP) following wet impregnation: Metal chlorides coordinated with 1,10-Phenanthroline loaded on supports; quartz boat pushed into a 923 K furnace zone at 20 cm s−1 (reaching 923 K within 5 s); annealing for 120 min at 923 K under Ar (100 sccm) or H2 (100 sccm) for oxide supports. Test conditions: Electrochemical hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in 1 M KOH (pH 13.8) at 10 mA cm−2 and 100 mA cm−2; stability tested via chronopotentiometry for 150 h; structural characterization via HR-STEM, HAADF-STEM, EDX, XRD, XPS, and ICP-OES. Findings: HEA-NPs achieved a narrow size distribution of ~2 nm up to denary compositions at 923 K; FMBP ensures simultaneous pyrolysis of mixed precursors, preventing phase separation unlike fixed-bed pyrolysis (FBP) which yields phase-separated alloys; FeCoPdIrPt@GO exhibited an overpotential of 42 mV at 10 mA cm−2, lower than commercial Pt/C (64 mV); Mass activity of FeCoPdIrPt@GO at 100 mV overpotential was 9.1 mA μgPt, 26 times higher than Pt/C (0.35 mA μgPt); Long-term stability of 150 h maintained at 10 mA cm−2 with no obvious change in morphology or composition; Atomic ratio error in synthesized alloys was below 15%, confirmed by EDX and ICP-OES; Tafel slope for FeCoPdIrPt was 82 mV dec−1, indicating the fastest kinetics among tested samples. Mechanism: The rapid heating to 923 K within 5 s creates high supersaturation of monomers, leading to a small critical nucleus radius (r* = 0.313 nm) and low critical excess free energy (ΔGr* = 2.54 × 10−20 J). This thermodynamically favors the formation of small, homogeneous nuclei clusters without phase separation, whereas slower heating (FBP/SMBP) results in larger nuclei and phase segregation due to higher ΔGr*.. Limitations: The text notes that HEA-NPs with low loading (3 wt%) were too small for clear EDX mapping, requiring higher loading (10 wt%) for elemental analysis; also, annealing times of 30 min led to carbon wrapping, while 180 min caused significant particle growth.. Future work: The authors propose a scalable method for production of supported HEA-NPs and suggest the strategy opens a venue for synthesizing alloys with tunable compositions for applications in catalysis, chemical sensing, biology, and energy conversion.. Quote: "Fast moving bed pyrolysis strategy ensures the mixed metal precursors rapidly and simultaneously pyrolyzed at high temperatures, resulting in nuclei with a small size."
